task: Verify the bug fix: brand/item logos must appear on printed PDF tags (pdfTags.ts fetchBrandLogo + drawTag embedding), including per-size dimensions and graceful fallback when a brand has no logo or unavatar.io returns a non-image/404.

bugs.title: A7 tag sheet: rows 0 and 3 of the 2x4 grid are drawn off the physical A4 page (pre-existing, unrelated to the logo fix)
bugs.description: pdfTags.ts SPECS.A7 = {w:74,h:105,cols:2,rows:4}. generateTagsPdf computes originY = (297 - rows*h)/2 = (297 - 4*105)/2 = -61.5mm. Row0 tile therefore spans y=[-61.5, 43.5] (entirely/partly off the top of the A4 page) and row3 spans y=[253.5, 358.5] (off the bottom). Only rows 1-2 (y within [0,297]) are ever visible/printable. In practice this means half of every 8-tile A7 sheet (the 1st and 4th rows) silently vanishes off the page edges and is never printed — not a logo-specific issue, but it surfaced while geometrically validating the A7 7mm-logo criterion (4 seeded items: 2 landed in the off-page row0 and were unrenderable, 2 landed in the on-page row1 and rendered correctly).
bugs.evidence: Computed geometry (python): originY=-61.5 for A7. Confirmed empirically in pdf-logo-size-a7-7mm: with 4 Nike items at A7, pixel-sampling the expected logo box at row0 returned total=0 samples (coordinates fall outside the rendered canvas — off page), while row1 samples returned 49/49 red pixels (on-page, correct). This is reproducible and deterministic, independent of the logo mock.

bugs.title: fetchBrandLogo() trusts the Content-Type header from unavatar.io without validating the actual image bytes, and drawTag() hardcodes addImage(..., "PNG", ...) — a real brand logo served as a mislabelled non-PNG crashes the whole PDF generation instead of degrading gracefully
bugs.description: unavatar.io intermittently serves a Windows .ico favicon body (verified via curl: `file` reports 'MS Windows icon resource') while still sending `content-type: image/png` for nike.com. fetchBrandLogo() only checks `blob.type.startsWith('image/')`, which passes, then data-URLs the raw ICO bytes and caches them. drawTag() calls `pdf.addImage(logoDataUrl, "PNG", ...)` unconditionally. jsPDF's PNG decoder then throws 'Error: wrong PNG signature', which propagates out of generateTagsPdf and is caught by PrintTags.tsx's catch block, showing toast.error('Could not generate PDF') instead of a successful PDF — for ALL tiles on the sheet, not just the one with the bad logo. Reproduced once (real Nike lookup, unmocked) during regression testing; a same-scenario rerun against the live (non-deterministic) service succeeded, confirming the trigger is unavatar.io's own response variability rather than app state. The spec explicitly says a missing/404 logo should be skipped gracefully (and the fix's own 404 handling works correctly, verified in pdf-logo-404-fallback-then-success-after-reload) — but a 200-with-wrong-bytes response is not handled the same way and takes down the entire print job.
bugs.evidence: curl -sI 'https://unavatar.io/nike.com?fallback=false' -> 'content-type: image/png'; curl body saved and `file` reports 'MS Windows icon resource - 3 icons...'. Captured browser console error during the one failing run: "Error: wrong PNG signature at checkSignature (jspdf.js:5254) ... at PngDecoder.decode ... at E.API.processPNG", and the UI stayed on 'Open PDF for printing' with no 'PDF ready' toast ever appearing (timed out waiting for it).

action_items: The A7 off-page row bug (rows 0 & 3 vanish) is unrelated to this logo fix but is a real content-loss defect worth a follow-up SPECS.A7 fix (likely rows should be 2, not 4, to match A7's real 74x105mm physical size against A4; or originY math needs revisiting).

Consider validating decoded image bytes (e.g. via `createImageBitmap` catch, or checking the PNG magic number) before calling addImage, and wrapping the addImage call in its own try/catch so a bad third-party logo degrades to text-only instead of failing the whole sheet.

Backend test suite has 3 pre-existing unrelated failures (not part of this task's scope): test_appraise_robustness_and_gating / test_appraise_endpoint fail because /tmp/item.jpg fixture image is missing from this environment, and test_shops_seeded_data expects 14 shops but found 15 (accumulated seed data from prior iterations). Not touched since outside this task's criteria.

checks.criterion: A8 PDF with a known-brand item embeds a logo image per tile
checks.name: pdf-logo-embeds-nike-a8
checks.evidence: Intercepted unavatar.io via page.route returning a solid-red 8x8 PNG fixture. Created 16 fresh tscheck-pdflogo-a8-* items (brand=Nike) via API, drove /print-tags?size=A8, clicked print-sheet-button, captured the generated application/pdf Blob via a patched URL.createObjectURL, parsed with pdfjs-dist in-browser, rendered page1 to canvas at scale 4, and sampled the exact computed logo bounding box (derived from pdfTags.ts's own padding/cursor math, inset 1mm) on all 16 tiles: every tile reported 96% (24/25) sampled pixels matching the mock red (R>200,G<60,B<60). doc.numPages===1.

checks.criterion: A6 PDF logo size matches spec (10mm)
checks.name: pdf-logo-size-a6-10mm
checks.evidence: Same red-PNG intercept; 4 fresh tscheck-pdflogo-a6-* Nike items at size=A6. Sampled the full 10mm logo box (1.5mm inset) on all 4 tiles: each reported 90.6% (58/64) red pixels, confirming the LOGO_MM.A6=10 square is filled by the embedded image. doc.numPages===1.

checks.criterion: A7 PDF logo size matches spec (7mm)
checks.name: pdf-logo-size-a7-7mm
checks.evidence: Same red-PNG intercept; 4 fresh tscheck-pdflogo-a7-* Nike items at size=A7. The on-page tiles (row1, both columns -- row0 is off-page due to the unrelated A7 layout bug documented in bugs[]) each reported 100% (49/49) red pixels in the computed 7mm logo box, confirming LOGO_MM.A7=7. doc.numPages===1.

checks.criterion: Unbranded item renders without a logo and without errors
checks.name: pdf-unbranded-renders-text-only-no-logo
checks.evidence: 2 fresh tscheck-pdflogo-unbranded-* items (brand=Unbranded) at A8, with an active-but-unused unavatar.io route intercept to prove it is never hit (unavatarHits===0, since brandDomain('unbranded') returns null -- no fetch at all). PDF generated successfully (doc.numPages===1, toast 'PDF ready'). The computed would-be-logo region shows 0% mock-colour pixels on both tiles, while a full-tile ink-pixel count (317 and 352 ink px) confirms the title/price/barcode text still renders. Zero console/page errors captured.

checks.criterion: unavatar.io 404 (brand with no logo) is handled gracefully
checks.name: pdf-logo-404-fallback-then-success-after-reload
checks.evidence: 2 fresh tscheck-pdflogo-404-* items (brand='Nonexistentbrand987') at A8. Phase 1: intercepted unavatar.io with a 404 text/html response -- PDF still generated (numPages=1, toast shown), computed logo-box pixel scan on both tiles = 0% mock colour (logo skipped), and the only console message was Chrome's own benign 'Failed to load resource: 404' network log (not an app-level JS/page error -- the fetch's `!res.ok` branch correctly returns null without throwing). Phase 2: page.goto reload (clears the module-scoped LOGO_CACHE) + intercept swapped to the valid red PNG -- regenerating the SAME brand's tag now embeds the logo (97.9% red fill on both tiles), proving the earlier 404 did not permanently poison the cache for that brand key.

checks.criterion: Button + toast flow regression (iteration_28's print-sheet-button check, re-verified)
checks.name: print-sheet-button-generating-state-and-toast
checks.evidence: iteration_28's hardcoded fixture ids no longer resolve (confirmed via GET /api/inventory/<id> -> 404 'Item not found', i.e. cleaned up by prior test runs over time) -- updated the check to create its own 16 fresh tscheck-printbtn-* items (brand=Unbranded, so it never touches the flaky third-party unavatar.io -- logo correctness is already covered by the 5 checks above). Clicking print-sheet-button showed the 'Generating...' label (sawGenerating=true) with a spinner, then exactly 1 application/pdf Blob (genCalls=1) and exactly 1 window.open call (openCalls=1), the success toast 'PDF ready — open in your PDF viewer to print' appeared, and the button returned to 'Open PDF for printing'. print-tags-grid stayed visible throughout.
